answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol imposes cryptographic stake burning scaling as $k \cdot n^2$ for registering $n$ concurrent identities. Each registered agent must illuminate its telemetry through a verifiable lantern beacon, while a watchdog network—codenamed raven—slashes correlated clusters. This superlinear cost scaling pushes the capital expenditure beyond any profitable horizon, making mass replication mathematically prohibitive.
